1.explanation:
• lib/features/modeling/Modeling.js: its connect() method takes all attrs (including waypoints) and hands them directly to moddle, so a SequenceFlow businessObject ends up with a .waypoints property. That turns into an illegal XML attribute on export.
• lib/features/modeling/behavior/ReplaceConnectionBehavior.js: this behavior explicitly does modeling.connect(..., { type:…, waypoints: connection.waypoints.slice() }). Passing waypoints here into the semantic create call is the root cause of JS objects landing on the BPMN element.
• lib/features/modeling/BpmnUpdater.js: this is responsible for moving geometry into the BPMNDI layer, but it never strips a .waypoints array off the businessObject. We should remove or ignore businessObject.waypoints in BpmnUpdater.updateConnectionWaypoints (or earlier) so it isn’t serialized on the BPMN element.
1.bug_scenario: When you use the auto-place append (green rectangle drag) to create a new task off of an existing one, bpmn-js wires them together automatically. Because the connector has a 90° “elbow” in the middle, the internal model ends up carrying a raw JS‐object array of waypoints on the BPMN businessObject. When you export, those objects are stringified into “[object Object],…” and written as an illegal waypoints attribute on the <sequenceFlow> element instead of as BPMNDI <di:waypoint> children.
